description: We are a team of four from Bangladesh working on the challenge "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map." Our project is a web tool where an explorer draws a route on Mars and instantly gets a verdict: slope, distance, travel time, hazards, and energy cost.
summary:
Martialoy is a web-based Mars traverse and survival planner built for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. A user draws a route across Jezero Crater, chooses an explorer (a rover or a human astronaut), and receives a survival card: distance, slope, travel time, energy use, and a clear PASS or FAIL with the exact reason.

The same engine judges both explorers from a profile of parameters, and keeps their energy separate: electrical energy for a rover, suit power and metabolic effort for a human.

It matters because a wrong route on Mars can end a mission, and early route screening is hard when terrain, energy and risk live in separate tools.
details:
Martialoy is a Mars traverse and survival planning application designed to help users explore the challenges of moving across the Martian surface. Users select either a rover or a suited astronaut profile, draw a route on the map, and receive an estimate of the route’s distance, elevation gain, slope, travel time, and energy use. The app checks the route against the selected profile’s limits and identifies the segment that causes a route to fail. When a route fails, Martialoy can search for a lower-cost alternative path using terrain elevation data.

The project combines an interactive map with a transparent planning model. Its web interface is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre, and PMTiles. The calculation engine uses Python, FastAPI, and NumPy, with Rasterio for working with elevation data. The model samples elevation along a route, estimates slope and travel time, and calculates rover energy or astronaut suit energy and metabolic effort. These human energy values are reported separately. Users can also inspect the assumptions behind the estimates, including units and references, instead of receiving an unexplained pass-or-fail result.

Martialoy is designed to make Martian terrain data easier to explore and to show how terrain can affect route planning. The map can use locally cached basemap and elevation files, supporting offline demonstrations. A CRISM OLINDEX3 layer provides additional mineral context where its data are available; it indicates a possible olivine-like spectral signal and is not a confirmed mineral identification or a route-safety measure. The route and survival calculations use the elevation model and selected rover or astronaut profile, not the CRISM layer.

The team considered usability, offline access, traceable assumptions, data limitations, and the different constraints of robotic and human explorers. Martialoy is an educational planning tool, not a mission-ready navigation system: it does not model every real-world hazard, such as wheel slip, sand traps, weather, radiation, or detailed astronaut physiology.
